jobs.description:
About the position
A full-time researcher position (SKO 1109) is available at the Center for Lifespan Changes in Brain and Cognition (LCBC), Department of Psychology (PSI), Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. The researcher will work full time on the Horizon Europe project SHIELD - Sources of Health Inequalities from Environmental Pollution in Lifespan Brain Development, funded by the Horizon Europe programme. SHIELD investigates how environmental exposures affect brain health and brain diseases across the entire lifespan, from conception to old age. 

The position will focus on environmental exposure modelling and the generation of environmental exposure maps for the SHIELD cohorts, as well as MRI data analysis. We are particularly looking for a candidate who can work at the interface of brain imaging and environmental exposure data, with a strong research background in MRI data analysis and experience with using environmental and geographic databases. Transdisciplinary experience and interest will be an advantage, as the consortium involves partners from multiple fields, including (but not limited to) psychology, medicine, physics, environmental epidemiology and statistical modelling. 
 
As SHIELD is expected to generate significant impacts, the researcher will be expected also to contribute to stakeholder engagement and science communication activities, for example by participating in stakeholder workshops and contributing to policy briefs, newsletters, and social media posts. 

The research position is funded until the end of the project, 31 December 2031. LCBC is the coordinator of the SHIELD consortium, which includes 13 partners, and this position will be one of the key roles in the entire consortium. The position and its associated tasks are funded only for the stated period and will end when the funding period expires.
More about the position and the research center
The goal of LCBC is to understand differences and changes in brain and cognition across the entire lifespan, and to identify how brain function and cognition can be optimized. LCBC is an active, multidisciplinary research center with around 25 full-time staff members, including four professors, two researchers, several postdoctoral fellows and PhD candidates, chief and senior data engineers, full- and part-time research assistants, administrative support, and several affiliated international researchers. 

LCBC has excellent research infrastructure, including access to a 3T Siemens Prisma MRI scanner, PET and EEG facilities, and comprehensive neuropsychological and somatic testing facilities. English is the main working language at the center.

LCBC has secured several large grants, including four European Research Council (ERC) grants, a Horizon 2020 grant, and several grants from the Research Council of Norway, the National Health Association of Norway, and the University of Oslo. In 2015, the group was designated “world-leading” and is one of only five such groups at the University of Oslo. More information is available on the LCBC website: https://www.lcbc.uio.no. 
Your main tasks will be
• Processing and analyzing multimodal brain MRI (structural, diffusion, and quantitative imaging) and cognitive trajectory and modeling these in relation to exposures. 
• Processing and analyzing behavioral and health data and modeling these in relation to brain and exposure data. 
• Characterizing and modelling historical air pollution concentrations (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, etc.) for the SHIELD cohorts by integrating Chemical Transport Model (CTM) simulation outputs with emission inventories and observational datasets. 
• Generating environmental exposure maps extending back to 1920 by combining diverse open-source datasets (meteorological, emissions, and land-use data) for SHIELD's Age-Period-Cohort (APC)-corrected analyses.
• Contribute to harmonization, expansion and application of EXPANSE maps. 
• Collaborate with other SHIELD researchers and participate in the SHIELD consortium meetings. 
• Write and publish scientific articles. 
• Contribute to stakeholder engagement and science communication activities of SHIELD: participating at workshops, writing policy-briefs, newsletters, social media posts etc.Qualifications
In this role you must have 

• PhD in a relevant field such as Neuroscience, Meteorology, Physics, Biophysics, Complex systems, Data Modelling, or a highly related, quantitative natural science/interdisciplinary field. 
• Research experience in Computational Neuroimaging analysis (structural, functional, diffusion, or quantitative MRI). 
• Experience with the use of meteorological/climate, spatial, or similar multidimensional databases. 
• Strong programming skills in Python and/or R. 
• Very good proficiency in written and spoken English is a prerequisite. 
It is an advantage if you have

• Experience with secure computing and data-handling environments suitable for sensitive human cohort data. 
• Experience with research in interdisciplinary/transdisciplinary research environments. 
• Experience in science communication and outreach activities.Personal qualities
In the evaluation of applicants, emphasis will be placed on the following personal skills: 

• Cooperation skills, and the ability to successfully join an international academic collaboration. 
• Professional and personal ability to work independently.   
In assessing applications, particular emphasis will be placed upon the quality of the candidate's academic qualifications. Interviews with selected candidates will be arranged where the applicant's prerequisites, interest in and motivation for the field of research, and cooperative skills will be assessed. 
We need different perspectives in our work 
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
We offer
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Committed, highly competent colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities. 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Researcher, position code 1109 in salary range NOK 720 000 - 820 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.
Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.

Planned start date: 1st April 2027.
Application
Your application should include:

• Letter of application, 1-2 pages, explaining the motivation for applying.
• Curriculum Vitae summarizing education, positions, and academic work.
• Copies of educational certificates, publications/academic work (if any) that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee.

This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information

As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews.
 
Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.Please refer to  Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and Rules for the use of research posts SKO 1108, 1109, 1110 and 1183 at UiO.

jobs.occupation: Product Manager
jobs.description:
We're looking for a product manager to own our product, from choosing which problems we solve to making sure customers use what we build. 

Bsure is one of Europe's fastest-growing startups, and we're proud of it. The tl;dr is that we work in cybersecurity. The slightly longer version is that we build a solution that finds and closes the security gaps in companies' identity landscapes. Think abandoned guest accounts, forgotten admin accounts or agents gone rogue. Many of these gaps also cost money in licenses nobody uses, so Bsure quickly becomes a cost tool too.

We're around 15 people in Norway and Sweden, with customers in the Nordics and the US. Our working languages are Norwegian and English.

You own the product direction and have the final say on priorities
You'll be responsible for the product, and for doing whatever it takes to make it a success. Defining what success means is part of the job too. Whatever it looks like, you need to love nerding out about the product, the industry and, above all, our customers. And you need to be motivated to set up a flow for product discovery and product delivery that gets results.

Product management is a broad role in itself, and it doesn't get any narrower in a startup. That's why you'll work closely with

• 
the developers and our CTO, who leads the tech team and sets the technical direction

• 
our UX designer, who designs the screens and the flow in the app

• 
Customer Value, who know our customers and follow up on usage

• 
sales and marketing, who are out talking to the market every single day

The role has no direct reports. We believe a role says something about what you're responsible for, but that doesn't mean you have to do everything yourself. Here we work toward one shared, hairy goal and allocate our resources accordingly.

You talk to customers every week and follow solutions all the way through
Here are some of your most important tasks:

• 
Understand customers. You regularly interview customers and people who aren't customers yet. You find out where it hurts, what they call it and what they do about it today.

• 
Facilitate product discovery. You lead discovery sessions with the team, keep track of hypotheses and opportunities, and bring the developers along to meet customers.

• 
Test before we build. Concepts, sketches and prototypes meet customers before they go into development. You use AI tools to get faster from idea to something customers can react to.

• 
Prioritize what we solve. You balance new opportunities, improvements to what we already have, technical needs and requests from individual customers, and you stand by your choices.

• 
Make the problem clear. You describe the problem, why it matters and what good enough looks like, so the developers can shape the solution in our Shape Up cycle.

• 
Follow the solution until it's in use. A shipped feature is a milestone. You follow up until customers use it and the value can be measured.

• 
Give the rest of Bsure good answers. Your insight gives sales and marketing the language they need.

You've done the job before, whatever the title was
You might come from product, service design, UX, business development or technology. You don't need to have held the "Product Manager" title before, but we're looking for someone with:

• 
product experience, where you've owned priorities and made decisions

• 
experience with qualitative interviews and service design methods, like customer journeys and service blueprints

• 
a steady hand as a facilitator, even when the room is full of experts

• 
structured thinking and clear writing

• 
business sense and an interest in how Bsure creates value for customers

• 
a good working relationship with developers, and the ability to talk workflows and integrations without writing the code yourself

• 
the ability to work comfortably in both Norwegian and English

What matters most to us is drive. If you're hungry to build something, learn fast and enjoy the pace of a startup, you're who we're looking for, whether you've been at it for three years or ten.

You'll pick up the identity and security knowledge with us.

It's a plus if you've worked at a startup, or with B2B SaaS for IT or security.

What success looks like after 6 to 12 months
• 
Product direction is built on customer insight, and the whole team can explain why we're building what we're building next.

• 
You have a steady rhythm for customer conversations and discovery, and the developers are part of it.

• 
What we launch gets used, and you can show it with numbers.

• 
The developers and the UX designer love working with you, because it's always clear what needs solving and why.

• 
You're known for bringing clarity, speed and structure wherever you go, sales and marketing included.

Why work at Bsure?
On top of joining a (by our own account) brilliant team in a varied and innovative environment, we can offer

• 
the chance to shape the product while a lot is still open, with more than 150 paying customers already using it

• 
a big opportunity for career growth, because you'll help shape a company building a product in a category Gartner has only recently defined

• 
a competitive salary and the possibility of stock options

• 
short decision paths, and founders who want to be challenged

A few famous last words
Joining Bsure is pretty special. You're coming in at the start of an adventure we think is going to be absolutely wild. We're helping shape the future of identity security. It might not be the conversation starter you bring to the dinner table, but the industry is groundbreaking, and we're at the front of it.

Bsure was started by five founders with an average of 20 years of domain experience. We've built what we wished had existed back when we worked in-house.

And the problems you'll work on, the team you'll work with and the opportunities you'll be exposed to will give you more than enough to talk about at the dinner table.

We review applications as they come in, and the deadline is December 31.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
At Bsure we build software that finds the security gaps companies don’t know they have. Abandoned guest accounts, forgotten admin accounts, AI agents nobody owns and licenses nobody uses.

More than 250 organizations in the Nordics and the US already use it, and in 2026 Sifted named us one of Europe’s fastest-growing startups. 

We’re around 15 people in Norway and Sweden, started by five founders with an average of 20 years in the field. That means short decision paths, real responsibility from day one and plenty of room to shape both the product and the company. If you like hard problems and want to see your work used by real customers, you’ll fit right in.

jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Ved Institutt for helse- og omsorgsfag (IHO), Det helsevitenskapelige fakultet er det en ledig stilling som stipendiat tilknyttet prosjektet RehabLos Kraftsenter – muligheter, barrierer og gevinster.

Generell informasjon om stillingen.

Stillingen gjelder for en periode på fire år. Ph.d.-studiet er normert til tre år. Det fjerde året, fordelt med 25 % pr år, skal brukes til undervisning ved bachelor og/eller masterprogrammene ved IHO som er relevant ut fra søkerens bakgrunn fra utdanning og praksisfelt. Stipendiatstillingen er en utdanningsstilling og har fullført forskerutdanning frem til doktorgrad som mål. Opptak til doktorgradsprogram er en forutsetning for ansettelse og studieperioden starter ved tiltredelse i stillingen. Mer informasjon om søknadsprosessen og ph.d.-forskrift finner du på Det helsevitenskapelige fakultets nettside.

Arbeidssted er UiT Norges arktiske universitet, ved campus Tromsø. Stillingen er ledig for tiltredelse, og du må kunne starte i stillingen innen rimelig tid etter å ha mottatt tilbud.
Om prosjektet / Stillingens forskningsområde
Er du sykepleier med interesse for rehabilitering? Liker du å samarbeide med andre for å utvikle og forbedre praksis? Da er denne stipendiatstillingen midt i blinken for deg!

RehabLos er et forsknings- og samskapingsprosjekt med overordnet mål om å utvikle en tverrfaglig, sektorovergripende og digitalstøttet rehabiliteringsmodell som styrker egenmobilisering og samfunnsinkludering for personer med ervervet hjerneskade og andre med komplekse rehabiliteringsbehov og deres pårørende. I prosjektet har vi fått finansiering for å utvikle og etablere RehabLos kraftsenter.

Kraftsenteret skal være et fysisk og digitalt senter som samler og koordinerer små og fragmenterte kompetansemiljøer og kobler sivilsamfunnet, lokalt engasjement og offentlige tjenester sammen på nye måter gjennom samskaping av kompetanse og tjenester. Konkrete lavterskeltilbud og digitale løsninger for bedre livsvilkår, helse, mestring og samfunnsinkludering (LMS) skal utprøves. Kraftsenteret skal også etablere et fagnettverk i samarbeid med de fire USHT-ene i regionen for å øke rehabiliteringskompetanse til de involverte aktørene i nedslagsfeltene.
 
PhD prosjektet skal følge etableringen av Kraftsenteret og identifisere muligheter, barrierer og ønsket innhold for lærings- og mestringstilbud for målgruppen. Det foreligger allerede innsamlet datamateriale fra fokusgruppeintervjuer som stipendiaten skal analysere for å utforske hvilke strukturelle, organisatoriske og faglige barrierer som må overskrides for å muliggjøre en integrert rehabiliteringsmodell som fremmer egenmestring og samfunnsinkludering. Stipendiaten skal også gjøre feltarbeid og gjennomføre fokusgruppeintervju for å følge etableringen av Kraftsenteret og identifisere nytte, gevinster og barrierer for implementering av LMS-tilbudene og fagnettverket gjennom Kraftsenteret.

RehabLos- prosjektet vektlegger brukermedvirkning og metoden som benyttes involverer aktiv deltakelse av både brukere, utøvere i helsetjenestene og andre relevante aktører. I dette innovative følgeforskningsprosjektet vil stipendiaten inngå i et tett og gjensidig forpliktende forskningssamarbeid med andre stipendiater, seniorforskere og praksisfelt. Forskningsarbeidet vil være knyttet til Forskningsgruppen Senter for omsorgsforskning, nord. Mer informasjon om forskningsgruppen finners her.
Kontakt
Flere opplysninger om stillingen kan du få av prosjektleder/førsteamanuensis Astrid Gramstad:

• telefon: +47 776 60 621
• e-post: astrid.gramstad@uit.no Kvalifikasjoner
For stillingen kreves:

• Norsk autorisasjon som sykepleier
• Relevant mastergrad innenfor helsefag eller andre relevante fagområder. Fullført mastergrad er en betingelse for å tiltre i stillingen. Du kan fortsatt søke dersom du er i sluttfasen av din mastergrad, men dokumentert fullført mastergrad er en betingelse for å tiltre i stillingen.

I vurderingen vil vi også vektlegge personlig egnethet og motivasjon for stillingen. Vi søker kandidater som blant annet har:

Opptak til ph.d.-program
For ansettelse som stipendiat er det en forutsetning at du blir tatt opp til ph.d.-programmet ved Det helsevitenskapelige fakultet og at du deltar i organiserte doktorgradsstudier i ansettelsesperioden.

• Masteroppgave med et omfang tilsvarende 20 studiepoeng eller mer hvis søkeren har en integrert mastergrad på 300 studiepoeng.

For søkere med utenlandsk utdanningsbakgrunn vil det vurderes om utdanningen likestilles med norsk høyere utdanning på mastergradsnivå. UiT Norges arktiske universitet har et personalpolitisk mål om å være en arbeidsgiver som gjenspeiler mangfoldet i samfunnet og som tar i bruk potensialet i befolkningens samlede kompetanse. Vi mener at inkludering og mangfold er en styrke og ønsker oss medarbeidere med ulik kompetanse, fagkombinasjoner, livserfaring og perspektiver.   

Har du funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn, oppfordrer vi deg som søker til å krysse av for dette i jobbsøkerportalen. Er det kvalifiserte søkere, kaller vi inn minst én i hver gruppe til intervju, og får du jobben, legger vi til rette for deg om du trenger det. Utenom å velge ut riktige kandidater bruker vi ikke avkrysningene til noe annet enn anonymisert statistikk. Les mer i Arbeidsgiverportalen: arbeidsgiver.difi.no/positivsaerbehandling

• Du blir en del av et spennende forskningsprosjekt

Vær oppmerksom på at søknaden kun vurderes basert på informasjonen som er sendt inn innen søknadsfristen via Jobbnorge. Det er derfor viktig at du legger ved alle nødvendige dokumenter som viser dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen.

Søknaden din må inneholde:

• Offisielle karakterutskrifter for bachelor- og mastergrad på originalspråk

Du må legge ved et utkast av oppgaven og en uttalelse fra veileder eller institusjonen om når det forventes at oppgaven er ferdig. Du må levere karakterutskrifter for graden, selv om den ikke er fullført.

All dokumentasjon som skal vurderes må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Hvis dokumentasjon på engelskkunnskaper mangler på søknadstidspunktet, må det dokumenteres før tiltredelse. 
Bedømmelse
Søkerne vil bli vurdert av en sakkyndig komité. Komiteens mandat er å foreta en vurdering av søkernes kvalifikasjoner på grunnlag av søknadsdokumentene og kunngjøringsteksten. Alle søkere vil motta en kopi av vurderingen til den sakkyndige komitéen. 

Søkere som vurderes å være best kvalifisert vil bli innkalt til intervju. Intervjuet skal blant annet avklare personlig egnethet og motivasjon for stillingen. 
Generell informasjon 
Ansettelsen skjer i henhold til regler og vilkår som til enhver tid gjelder for statsansatte, og retningslinjer ved UiT. På våre nettsider finner du mer informasjon til søkere på stillinger ved UiT.

Fra lønnen blir det trukket 2% innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.Du vil bli medlem i Statens pensjonskasse, som gir deg mange goder i tillegg til livsvarig alderspensjon og AFP: Du kan ha rett til økonomisk støtte hvis du blir syk eller ufør, familien din kan ha rett til økonomisk støtte når du dør, du blir forsikret mot yrkesskade eller yrkessykdom, og du får gode betingelser på boliglån. Personopplysninger som oppgis behandles i henhold til lov om behandling av personopplysninger. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Economics of Education
jobs.description:
The Research Department of Statistics Norway invites applications for a two-year fixed-term position in economics, funded by the Research Council of Norway through "Match effects and matchmaking in education" (MatchEd, project no. 358940). The position is based in Oslo, Norway, with an anticipated starting date of September 1, 2027.  The Research Department conducts economic research using extensive Norwegian administrative data. The department has an established group of researchers working in applied microeconomics, including the economics of education, and close connections with the University of Oslo and the international research community.  About the project  MatchEd explores how the assignment of students to schools, programs, and tracks affects academic outcomes, motivation, and equality of opportunity. Beyond estimating whether some schools or programs benefit particular students more than others (match effects), the project aims to identify the mechanisms behind this heterogeneity, and to translate these insights into evidence-based guidance for designing fairer and more effective assignment systems. The project exploits centralized admission systems (e.g., deferred acceptance with priority-based cutoffs) linked to population-wide registers.  The project is led by Edwin Leuven (Statistics Norway and the University of Oslo) and Sturla Løkken (Statistics Norway).  
Job descriptionThe successful candidate will conduct empirical research using Norwegian administrative data and collaborate with other project members on research papers intended for publication in international economics journals. The position provides opportunities to pursue original research within the scope of the project, with no teaching obligations.   Qualifications
Applicants will be evaluated primarily on research potential, the quality of their research, and the relevance of their interests to the project.  Candidates should have:  

• A PhD in economics or a closely related field, completed by the starting date. Candidates who expect to complete their PhD before taking up the position are welcome to apply. 
• Strong training in applied microeconometrics, particularly causal inference.  
• Experience working with and analyzing individual-level microdata.  
• The ability to conduct independent research and collaborate effectively with other researchers.

About the position
The Department of Education at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position in Educational Psychology. We seek applicants with a strong research interest in counselling practices targeting schools, Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) settings, and/or Educational Psychological Counselling settings. 

Educational systems in Norway and internationally face growing challenges concerning inclusion, diversity, and equity. Addressing these challenges requires stronger collaboration across the education system, including early childhood education and care (ECEC), schools, and support services. It also calls for closer links between research and practice, to improve educational quality and learning outcomes. We are seeking applicants with a research portfolio in these areas. 

The position is suited for candidates who wish to advance research on counselling, implementation processes, and/or organizational development. We particularly encourage applicants whose research focuses on inclusion in educational communities. Relevant experience includes experimental interventions and longitudinal studies involving families or educational settings and examining the conditions that support learning, development, well-being, and engagement. 

We welcome diverse scholarly profiles but particularly value innovative, methodologically rigorous research. Expertise in quantitative methods will be emphasised, while experience integrating qualitative approaches, such as observation of collaboration and interaction, is an advantage. Experience leading large-scale projects, managing complex project structures or coordinating interdisciplinary teams will be valued.

The position involves 47 % teaching, 47 % research, and 6 % administrative tasks.
More about the position
The successful candidate is expected to strengthen research in educational psychology and contribute to the Faculty of Educational Sciences’ research group, Development, Equity and Literacy in Learning Contexts (DEAL). 

The successful candidate is also expected to actively participate in the collective development of our education programs and teach at the bachelor- and master-level programs in Educational Psychology.

The candidates’ scientific production in the past 5 years will be emphasized in the assessment. It is expected that the successful candidate publishes internationally and seeks external funding.

The appointee must be able to lead and initiate research, supervise doctoral degree students, participate in teaching and examination work at all levels, and undertake administrative tasks, in accordance with applicable provisions. 

More specifically the appointee must:

• Contribute to the development of research and study programs in Educational Psychology

• Success in obtaining grants for major research applications and experience in leading and completing research projects. The research should be of high quality, demonstrating both breadth and depth within the research field and showing the ability to address new issues.

jobs.description:
The position
A 4-year PhD position in Evolutionary Biochemistry is available at the Department of Medical Biology, Faculty of Health Sciences, within the Host–Microbe Interaction (HMI) research group. The position is part of the LacZymes project, led by Dr. Christopher Frøhlich.

General information about the position.

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD programme is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25 % each year and will consist of teaching and other duties. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to the PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The project 
Do you hold a Master’s degree in molecular biology (or a related field) and have a strong interest in the molecular mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance development? Are you motivated to conduct interdisciplinary research at one of the northernmost universities in the world? If so, this PhD position may be of interest to you.

The successful candidate will join a project aiming to uncover the molecular mechanisms of AMR evolution at the enzymatic level. To address this, the project integrates ancestral sequence reconstruction, directed evolution, pre-steady-state and steady-state enzyme kinetics, and X-ray crystallography. Candidates with experience in one or more of these areas are encouraged to apply.

The PhD candidate will report to Dr. Christopher Frøhlich and is expected to contribute actively to the project while developing expertise at the interface of molecular biology, enzymology, and evolutionary biology.

The PhD candidate will work on the following tasks: 

• Manage their own research project
• Experimental design and execution
• Enzyme evolution and selection
• Enzyme production and purification
• Biochemical enzyme characterization
• Structural and functional characterization
• Writing scientific papers and a PhD thesis
• Presenting the work in national and international arenas 
Personal characteristics:The applicant should be motivated, creative and ambitious, with a strong ability to work problem-solution orientated both in teams and independently. The applicant should be genuinely interested in the field of molecular evolution and AMR as well as scientific dissemination. In the evaluation of which applicant is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience, and personal suitability, in terms of the qualification requirements specified in this position announcement. The appointment is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants and national guidelines for appointment as PhD fellow

Applicants are required to submit a motivation letter describing how the position aligns with their research interests.
Contact
For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Christopher Frøhlich:

• phone: +47 46 96 87 78
• email: christopher.frohlich@uit.noQualifications
Required qualifications

• Master’s degree in molecular biology, microbiology, chemistry or equivalent education, with a grade of C or better. Candidates who have not yet completed their Master’s education must submit a written statement from their main supervisor stating the tentative date of their Master’s defence.
• Experience in at least two of the following areas: molecular cloning, protein expression and purification, biochemical characterization of enzymes (e.g. kinetic investigations), X-ray crystallography
• Documented oral and written English skills
Applicants must document fluency of in English and be able to work in an international environment. Nordic applicants can document their English capabilities by attaching their high school diploma.  Working knowledge of Norwegian or a Scandinavian language is also beneficial.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience in the field of AMR and AMR mechanisms
• Experience in coding (e.g. Python) and competence with computer-based analytical tools (e.g., Pymol)
• Knowledge of a Scandinavian language
• Experience in writing publications
• Experience in a biosafety level-2 laboratory environment
In the assessment, the emphasis is on the applicant's potential to complete a research education based on the master's thesis or equivalent, and any other scientific work. (The motivation letter will also be considered.) In addition, professional experience and other experience of significance for the completion of the doctoral programme will be taken into consideration.

We will also emphasize motivation and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have good collaboration skills
• Have good communication and interaction with colleagues and students
• Wants to contribute to a good working environment
As many people as possible should have the opportunity to undertake organized research training. If you already hold a PhD or have equivalent competence, we will not appoint you to this position.
Admission to the PhD programme 
For employment in the PhD position, you must be qualified for admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Health Sciences and participate in organized doctoral studies within the employment period.

Admission normally requires:  

• A bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS and a master's degree of 120 ECTS, or an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 30 ECTS for a master's degree of 120 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 20 ECTS for an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
 
 
Applicants must have a grade of C or better on the master's thesis and have a grade point average of C or better for the master's degree. A more detailed description of admission requirements can be found here.

If you are employed in the position, you will be provisionally admitted to the PhD programme. Application for final admission must be submitted no later than two months after taking up the position. 

Applicants with a foreign education will be subjected to an evaluation of whether the educational background is equal to Norwegian higher education, following national guidelines from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills. Depending on which country the education is from, one or two additional years of university education may be required to fulfil admission requirements, e.g. a 4-year bachelor's degree and a 2-year master's degree. UiT normally accepts higher education from countries that are part of the Lisbon Recognition Convention.
Inclusion and diversity
UiT The Arctic University of Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity are a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite at least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.
We offer
• Involvement in an interesting research project 
• Good career opportunities 
• A good academic environment with dedicated colleagues  
• Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
• Pension scheme through the state pension fund 
• PhD Fellows are normally given a salary of 580 000 NOK/year with a 3% yearly increase
Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information about working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility
Application 
Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include: 

• A motivation letter describing how this position aligns with the applicant’s research interests.
• CV, including a list of publications, if applicable. 
• Official diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language 
• Official transcripts of grades/academic record for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language
• Official translation of diplomas and transcripts of records (ToR) to English or a Scandinavian language, if applicable
• Explanation of the grading system for foreign education (Diploma Supplement if available)
• Documentation of English proficiency
• Two references with contact information
Qualification with a master’s degree is required before commencement in the position. If you are near completion of your master’s degree, you may still apply and submit a statement from your supervisor or institution indicating when the degree will be obtained. You must still submit your transcript of grades for the master’s degree with your application.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 
Assessment 
The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. 
General information 
The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants. 

Remuneration for the position of PhD Fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017. A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension: You may be entitled to financial support if you become ill or disabled, your family may be entitled to financial support when you die, you become insured against occupational injury or occupational disease, and you can get good terms on a mortgage. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.
 
A shorter period of appointment may be decided when the PhD Fellow has already completed parts of their research training programme or when the appointment is based on a previous qualifying position PhD Fellow, research assistant, or the like in such a way that the total time used for research training amounts to three years. 

We process personal data given in an application or CV in accordance with the Personal Data Act (Offentleglova). According to the Personal Data Act information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. You will receive advance notification in the event of such publication, if you have requested non-disclosure.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position  - in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG)
jobs.description:
About the position 
A PhD research fellowship is available in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG) at the Institute of Oral biology, Faculty of Dentistry, the University of Oslo. One of our group’s major interests is the study of how extracellular vesicles from cancer cells affect various normal cells, both in the immediate vicinity of the tumor and at a distance, changing their phenotype to support the growing tumor mass. In the proposed project, we aim to investigate the effect of extracellular vesicles from oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) on the function of normal cells, including endothelial cells. 
 
The candidate will apply various experimental methods to assess whether the normal phenotype changes towards a tumor-supporting one upon OSCC-derived extracellular vesicle exposure. Such alterations may include increased proliferation, modifications of intracellular Ca2+ signalling pathways, shifts in the metabolic profile and more.     
More about the position
The main purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

Project title: “Tumor-host interaction in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)”

This is a 100% full-time, three-year PhD Research Fellowship position. The successful candidate is expected to produce three scientific papers and a doctoral thesis. The place of work is Oslo, Norway.
More about the fellowship
Admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Dentistry is a prerequisite for taking up the position. The candidate is expected to complete the project within the fellowship period. A final plan for the research training must be approved and formalised no later than three months after the start of the position.

The main supervisor will be Professor Trude Marie Haug - Institute of Oral Biology
Qualification requirements
Mandatory requirements

• Applicants must hold a Master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree in molecular biology, cell biology, dentistry or in another field relevant to the research project.
• The Master’s thesis must have a grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system.
• A good level of written and oral communication skills in English is required.
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements: https://www.odont.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/supplementary-rules.html
• Publications in international peer-reviewed scientific journals will be advantageous but not required
Experience in the following methods will be advantageous:

• Cell culturing
• Standard molecular biological techniques and immunohistochemistry
• Analysis of -omics data
• Intracellular Ca2+ imagingPersonal skills:
• Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary scientific environment
• Self-motivation, creativity, genuine curiosity about the subject, work discipline, professional ethics, and ambition
• Strong practical and analytical skills
• Good social and collaboration skills
We need different perspectives in our work

• UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that aims to provide an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. We fulfil our mission most effectively when we draw on different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives.
• We will do our best to accommodate individual needs. Relevant adjustments may include adaptations to working hours, tasks, digital or physical tools, or other practical measures. Applicants with an immigrant background, a disability or gaps in their CV are encouraged to indicate this in the application portal. UiO invites at least one qualified applicant from each of these groups to interview in accordance with applicable state-sector procedures.Why should you choose us?
• A clearly defined and fully funded three-year PhD project with established core infrastructure.
• Dedicated supervision and research-training.
• An interdisciplinary and internationally connected research environment at the Faculty of Dentistry.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities, good welfare schemes and up to 1.5 hours per week of exercise during working hours.(Good welfare schemes)
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens Pensjonskasse), with beneficial pension, mortgage and insurance arrangements.
• Oslo’s family-friendly environment, with extensive cultural and outdoor opportunities.
• Dedicated mentoring and a professionally stimulating working environment.
• Salary in position as Doctoral Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 551000 - to 605000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.
Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
How to apply
Your application must include:

• A cover letter of 1-2 pages describing your motivation for the position, your relevant academic and practical experience, and how your background matches the project.
• A CV summarizing education, work experience, research experience and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of diplomas, academic transcripts and certificates. Applicants should retrieve available results from Vitnemålsportalen; where this is not possible, copies must be uploaded.
• Documentation of English proficiency where required under the Faculty’s supplementary admission rules.
• A complete list of publications and other academic work, if applicable, together with the work the applicant wishes the evaluation committee to consider.
• A copy of your master thesis if possible.
• Contact information for two to three references, including name, position, relationship to the applicant, e-mail address and telephone number.
• The application and all attachments must be submitted through UiO’s electronic recruitment system, Jobbnorge, by clicking “Apply for the position”. All documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language. Applicants with education from outside Scandinavia should include an explanation of their university’s grading system and a Diploma Supplement where available. A recognition statement from the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), if already obtained, may also be attached.
• Particular emphasis will be placed on documented academic qualifications, relevant experimental competence, motivation and personal suitability. The best-qualified candidates will be invited to interview and may be asked to give a brief presentation of previous research or technical work.General information
Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.
 
Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian),  Guidelines concerning appointment to post doctoral and research posts at UiO and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.

Guidelines concerning appointment to recruitment positions at UiO - University of Oslo

Doctoral degree: PhD in Dentistry - Faculty of Dentistry

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology, and services).
